question: Must this availability-sensitive Android lifecycle fix show emulator or physical-device process-death proof before merge, or is the source contract plus Robolectric coverage sufficient?
rationale: Repository policy makes real behavior proof a gate for external PRs, while a maintainer could explicitly accept the remaining Android platform uncertainty.

options.title: Require real lifecycle proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until a redacted emulator or physical-device run demonstrates sticky recreation, Gateway reconnection, terminal STOP, and clean app reconnection.

options.title: Accept simulated-only proof
options.body: Merge based on source review, Android service semantics, focused Robolectric coverage, and green Android CI while accepting residual platform lifecycle risk.

recommendation.title: Require real lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until a redacted emulator or physical-device run demonstrates sticky recreation, Gateway reconnection, terminal STOP, and clean app reconnection.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the persistent service/runtime architecture and has the strongest recent history across the affected Android lifecycle files.
